newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady around 3.05-3.10 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady around 3.05-3.10 pct.

text.p: German overnight call rates were little changed on Friday at around 3.05 percent to 3.10 percent as liquidity continued to return to normal at the start of the new month.

Traders said they expected rates to remain stable now after spiking sharply higher in late December as banks sought funds to meet reserve targets and companies borrowed overnight money for "window dressing" of their year-end books.
Banks held 51.9 billion marks with the Bundesbank on Tuesday, up from 48.9 billion marks on Monday, leaving the average for Decmeber at 41.1 billion marks.

Banks tapped the Bundesbank's 4.50 percent emergency Lombard lending facility for 600 million marks on Thursday, down from three billion marks they had borrowed the previous working day when money was still tight.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= stood at 3.11267 percent compared with 3.11867 percent.
